prompt: On Google Cloud, who runs the web server in front of a Python function?
hint: You write one function, not a program that listens.

choices.text: Your main.py, which must open port 8080 itself
choices.why: main.py only defines the function; nothing in it listens.

choices.text: A shared nginx that Google runs for every function in the region
choices.why: Each function is its own Cloud Run service with the framework inside.

choices.text: The Functions Framework
choices.why: Right. The same library you ran locally, in a container on Cloud Run.

choices.text: gunicorn, which you add to requirements.txt
choices.why: The build installs the framework; you add nothing to serve HTTP.

prompt: The quote function returned {"error": "POST a list of items"}, 405 for a GET. Who chose 405?
hint: Look at the return statement.

choices.text: The function, by returning a dictionary and the number 405
choices.why: Right. The framework turned the pair into a JSON body and a status.

choices.text: The framework, which allows only POST by default
choices.why: The framework passes every method to the function.

choices.text: curl, which reports 405 when it sends no body
choices.why: curl only prints the status the server sent.

choices.text: Cloud Run, which refuses GET on HTTP-triggered functions
choices.why: Nothing was deployed, and HTTP functions accept any method.

prompt: With PRICES = mug 3500, tee 7900, poster 2500 (cents), what total_cents does the quote function return for three posters and one mug?
A developer adds a module-level counter to the quote function to number each quote. In production the numbers repeat and skip. Why?
hint: How many copies of the module are there?

choices.text: Python integers overflow once the counter passes a few thousand calls
choices.why: Python integers do not overflow.

choices.text: The framework reloads main.py before every request
choices.why: The module is loaded once per instance, which is why PRICES is reused.

choices.text: Requests are retried, and each retry increments it twice
choices.why: An HTTP call is not retried by the platform; the copies are the problem.

choices.text: Each instance has its own counter, and instances start and stop
choices.why: Right. Anything that must survive a call belongs in a database or a queue.

prompt: The functions-framework flag that names the function inside main.py is --___.
hint: It points the framework at the function.

prompt: What does an event function return to say it succeeded?
hint: The framework reads one thing.

choices.text: The string OK
choices.why: The framework sends OK itself; the function returns nothing.

choices.text: Nothing; not raising is success
choices.why: Right. An exception becomes a 500, which is a failure.

choices.text: The number 200
choices.why: Statuses are for HTTP functions; an event function returns nothing.

choices.text: The event it received, unchanged
choices.why: Nothing is read from the return value.

prompt: Match each CloudEvent attribute to what it says.
hint: The four the curl call sent as headers.

pairs.right: This event, unique for its source

right_distractors: How many times it was delivered

prompt: A request to the notify function carried ce-type, ce-source and ce-specversion but no ce-id. What happened?
hint: Did the function's terminal print anything?

choices.text: The function ran with an empty id and printed it
choices.why: Its terminal showed one event, the first one.

choices.text: The framework invented an id and answered 200
choices.why: It answered 400; inventing ids would break deduplication.

choices.text: Framework said 400; the function never ran
choices.why: Right. Without an id it is not a CloudEvent.

choices.text: curl refused to send a request without the header
choices.why: curl sent it; the 400 came back from the framework.

prompt: Sending CloudEvent attributes as ce- headers with the data as the body is called the ___ content mode.
hint: The other mode is structured.

prompt: An event function catches every exception, logs it and returns normally, "so the logs stay clean". What does that cost on Google Cloud?
hint: What does a normal return tell the sender?

choices.text: Failures pass as successes, never retried
choices.why: Right. Catch what you handled and let the rest escape.

choices.text: Nothing; the event is retried anyway after a log entry
choices.why: Retries are decided by the status, and a normal return is a 2xx.

choices.text: The function is disabled after ten logged errors
choices.why: No such rule; it keeps receiving events.

choices.text: A 500 for every call, which is billed twice
choices.why: A normal return is a 2xx, not a 500.

prompt: How does a function with a Pub/Sub trigger receive messages?
hint: Who opens the connection?

choices.text: It keeps a connection open to the topic and reads from it
choices.why: Nothing listens to the topic; that is the common wrong picture.

choices.text: It pulls the subscription every few seconds
choices.why: A function does not poll; it is called.

choices.text: Pub/Sub writes each message to a file the function opens
choices.why: Delivery is an HTTP request, not a file.

choices.text: A push subscription POSTs each message to it over HTTP
choices.why: Right. The trigger is a subscription pointed at the function.

prompt: Why does the course use pubsub.py instead of gcloud pubsub against the emulator?
hint: What does gcloud check before anything else?

choices.text: gcloud cannot create push subscriptions at all
choices.why: It can, given an account; the account is the obstacle.

choices.text: gcloud needs an account; the library does not
choices.why: Right. With PUBSUB_EMULATOR_HOST set, the library needs no credentials.

choices.text: The emulator speaks a protocol gcloud never learnt
choices.why: The emulator speaks Pub/Sub's own API.

choices.text: pubsub.py is faster because it skips encryption
choices.why: Speed is not the reason; the account check is.

prompt: What stops pubsub.py from ever creating a topic in the real Pub/Sub?
hint: Read its first lines of main.

choices.text: The project id planner-dev, which Google refuses
choices.why: A project id is not a guard; the program checks something else first.

choices.text: The token no-account, which the library sends
choices.why: That variable is Terraform's; the library does not read it.

choices.text: It exits when PUBSUB_EMULATOR_HOST is not set
choices.why: Right. Without the variable the library would go to the real service.

choices.text: Docker's network, which has no route to Google
choices.why: pubsub.py runs on the laptop, not in a container.

prompt: Put the path of message 1042 in order, from the command to the printed line.
hint: Follow the figure from left to right.
items: The topic keeps a copy for the subscription orders-fn
The subscription POSTs it to localhost:8080
The framework turns the push into a CloudEvent
on_order decodes the base64 and prints the line

prompt: Where in the CloudEvent does on_order find the order number?
hint: It is encoded.

choices.text: In data.message.data, as base64
choices.why: Right. The function decodes it.

choices.text: In the ce-id header
choices.why: The id is the message id, 1, not the order.

choices.text: In the attribute source
choices.why: source carried web, the attribute that was set.

choices.text: In the URL of the push endpoint
choices.why: The endpoint is the same for every message.

prompt: What does the deployed version of this chain have that the laptop's did not? Choose all that apply.
hint: The section names the differences.

choices.text: An identity token proving the caller is Pub/Sub
choices.why: Right; the laptop's push carried none.

choices.text: A topic and subscription living in the project
choices.why: Right; here they lived in a container.

choices.text: A different payload format for the message
choices.why: The shape is the one you ran.

choices.text: A function that pulls instead of being pushed to
choices.why: It is still pushed to.

prompt: What does Google call the second generation of Cloud Functions now?
hint: Its name says what it is built on.

choices.text: App Engine functions
choices.why: App Engine is lesson 19's platform.

choices.text: Eventarc functions
choices.why: Eventarc delivers events; it does not run code.

choices.text: Cloud Functions Plus
choices.why: No such product.

choices.text: Cloud Run functions
choices.why: Right. Each one is a Cloud Run service with the framework inside.

prompt: A burst brings 300 simultaneous requests to a first-generation function. How many instances does it need at least?
hint: One request per instance.

prompt: Which limit is the same in both generations?
hint: One of the rows in the table does not change.

choices.text: The longest HTTP call
choices.why: 9 minutes against 60.

choices.text: The longest event call, 9 minutes
choices.why: Right. Only HTTP got the hour.

choices.text: Requests per instance
choices.why: One against up to 1,000.

choices.text: The largest instance you may ask for
choices.why: 8 GiB against 32 GiB.

prompt: A function calls its own URL by mistake for every request it receives. Which setting in main.tf bounds the damage?
hint: It is a ceiling on copies.

choices.text: timeout_seconds
choices.why: It limits one call, not how many run.

choices.text: available_memory
choices.why: Memory per instance does not bound instances.

choices.text: max_instance_count
choices.why: Right. It caps how far the loop can scale.

choices.text: entry_point
choices.why: It names the function, nothing more.

prompt: The plan printed uri = (known after apply). What would make it known?
hint: Who chooses the address?

choices.text: Deploying the function, because Google assigns the address then
choices.why: Right. Like an instance id, it is decided on the other side.

choices.text: Setting GOOGLE_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN to a real token and planning again
choices.why: A plan does not create the function; the address appears when it exists.

choices.text: Adding a uri line to service_config
choices.why: It is an output, not something you set.

choices.text: Running terraform init with the mirror again
choices.why: init installs the provider; it decides no addresses.

prompt: In gcloud functions deploy, the flag that turns an HTTP function into one fed by the Pub/Sub messages of orders is --trigger-___=orders.
hint: It names what feeds the function.

prompt: Order these by how many instances 200 simultaneous requests would need, from fewest to most.
hint: Divide by what one instance takes at once.
trap: The first generation takes one request per instance, so it needs all 200.

prompt: A team needs to resize product photos whenever one is uploaded. Which shape fits best?
hint: A small piece of work with a clear trigger.

choices.text: A Compute Engine machine polling the bucket every minute
choices.why: It pays all month to wait, and lags by up to a minute.

choices.text: An HTTP function the browser calls after uploading
choices.why: A closed tab would leave a photo unresized.

choices.text: A Cloud Run service with twenty routes
choices.why: One reaction does not need an application.

choices.text: An event function triggered by the upload
choices.why: Right. Lesson 18 wires exactly this.
